*[[Gaza–Israel conflict]]; [[Gaza–Israel clashes (November 2019)]]
**[[Israel|Israeli]] [[airstrike]]s leave 22 [[Palestinians]] (20 militants and 2 civilians) dead and dozens injured. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/gaza-israel-rockets-day-2-islamic-jihad-tel-aviv-hamas-syria-1.8122258 (''Haaretz'')]
**More than 200 rockets are fired into Israel from [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://nypost.com/2019/11/12/nearly-200-rockets-launched-at-israel-from-gaza-strip-since-killing-of-islamic-jihad-leader/ (''New York Post'')]
**An [[Islamic Jihad]] rocket commander and five relatives are killed in an Israeli airstrike. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/palestinians-say-family-of-6-killed-in-apparent-israeli-strike-on-home-in-gaza/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Islamist insurgency in Mozambique]], [[Mozambique–Tanzania relations]]
**[[Jihadist]]s kill six civilians and injure seven in a village near the [[Mozambique]]–[[Tanzania]] border. All the victims are Tanzanian nationals, while the terrorists are identified as Mozambicans. [https://www.news24.com/Africa/News/six-killed-in-tanzania-attack-near-border-with-mozambique-20191113 (News24)]
*[[Crime in Poland]]
**Two people are arrested in [[Poland]] for planning to kill [[Muslims]] in an attack [[Copycat crime|inspired]] by the [[2011 Norway attacks|2011 Utoya/Oslo attacks]] by [[Norwegians|Norwegian]] mass murderer [[Anders Behring Breivik]], and the [[Christchurch mosque shootings|Christchurch, New Zealand mosque shootings]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-poland-arrests/poland-seizes-two-for-plotting-breivik-style-attacks-on-muslims-idUSKBN1XN23L?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
* A bus collision with a truck near [[Nitra]] kills 13 people and leaves at least 17 wounded. The disaster is the deadliest in [[Slovakia]] in a decade. [https://www.reuters.com/article/slovakia-crash/bus-crash-in-slovakia-kills-at-least-13-many-more-injured-idUSL8N27T5DN (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[Japan–North Korea relations]], [[Japan–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea]]n media reports that between May and September, [[Japanese Prime Minister]] [[Shinzō Abe]] sent personal letters to [[North Korea]]'s [[Kim Jong-un]] to hold bilateral meetings to ease tensions between the two countries. A [[Japanese government]] spokesman denies the report. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2019/11/13/national/politics-diplomacy/abe-sent-personal-letters-holding-summit-kim-jong-un-south-korean-paper/#.XcwkDtIzZ6o (''The Japan Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases]] 
**The [[Australian High Court]] agrees to hear a final appeal from ex-[[Holy See|Vatican]] treasurer and convicted [[child sex offender]] [[George Pell]], who was found guilty of [[sexually assault]]ing three teenage choirboys. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-australia-abuse-pell/australian-high-court-agrees-to-hear-ex-vatican-treasurers-sex-offences-appeal-idUSKBN1XM2V6 (Reuters)]

*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**Hong Kong leader [[Carrie Lam]] vows not to give in to protesters as chaos continues into Wednesday morning. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/hong-kong-faces-more-transit-disruptions-after-chaotic-night (''The Straits Times'')]
**Schools, transport links and businesses close amid rising clashes in the city. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests/protesters-blockade-universities-business-district-as-chaos-grips-hong-kong-idUSKBN1XN04N (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]], [[Evo Morales government resignation]]
**Bolivia's exiled former [[President of Bolivia|president]] [[Evo Morales]] rejects the presidency of opposition senator [[Jeanine Áñez]], but police bar lawmakers from his party from entering the legislature to undo it. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/morales-supporters-reject-interim-president-deepening-bolivias-crisis/2019/11/13/8ff38680-061f-11ea-9118-25d6bd37dfb1_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**Two people were killed on in clashes between Bolivian police and supporters of former president Evo Morales. In total, 10 people have been killed so far since political turmoil broke out in Bolivia. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/killed-unrest-continues-bolivia-191114164711003.html (Al Jazeera)]
